arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Clark argued that retiree health benefits should be decided like other contract disputes.
Ms. Ho argued that unalterable benefits must be negotiated, not imposed by courts.
Justice Scalia questioned the advocate's stance on the parol evidence rule.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests how courts interpret collective bargaining agreements. The core issue is whether silence implies a permanent promise of retiree health benefits.

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on November 10, 2014.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 3, lines 7-15

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: M&G Polymers wants courts to apply ordinary contract principles without presumptions.
Retirees want courts to infer permanent benefits from contractual silence.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 24, lines 11-25

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: M&G Polymers argues that promises of costly benefits must be explicitly negotiated.
Retirees argue that the Sixth Circuit correctly inferred vested benefits from silence.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Sotomayor asked if the district court relied on a presumption.
Justice Kagan asked if the parties are disputing specific language rather than silence.
